bibliography.note: Havey, Keith A. 1973. Production of juvenile alewives, Alosa pseudoharengus, at Love Lake, Washington County, Maine. Transactions of the American Fisheries Society 102(2): 434–437 (Crossref's title has a stray comma, 'Love, Lake').

claims.claim: alewife in-lake adult mortality 90.7 % at Love Lake, Washington Co. (Havey 1973, via Fay et al. 1983)
claims.note: Havey not read. Fay et al. 1983 (PDF p. 20, Fayetal_1983.txt) relay: 'Total adult freshwater mortality averaged 90.7% and ranged from 66% to 100% over the 11-year study period (Havey 1973)'. The relay matches the paper; the 41 % in the same cell is Fay's relay of Havey 1961 (Long Pond, 'freshwater post-spawning mortality for all age groups averaged 41%', range 32–67 % over six years).

claims.claim: Love Lake (272 ha): 220–439,062 emigrants a year (up to ~1,600/ha; project arithmetic)
claims.note: Fay et al. relay 'The number of emigrants ranged from 220 to 439,062 fish over an 11-year study period' and 12–3,209 emigrants per female per year. Fay gives no lake area; the 272 ha comes from elsewhere. 439,062 / 272 = 1,614/ha, so '~1,600/ha' holds if the area is right.

claims.claim: Love Lake's emigrants correlated with escapement over 11 years
claims.note: Fay et al. relay significant linear relationships 'between the log of female escapement and the log of juvenile emigrant abundance', and between emigrant abundance and spawning-run size four years later.
